item.title: Escambia firefighters rescue 2 residents, 3 dogs from house fire

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Fire Rescue responded to a residential structure fire Tuesday, successfully evacuating two residents and three dogs from the burning home without any injuries, according to WKRG News 5.

Fire crews arrived at the scene and worked quickly to locate and remove the occupants and their pets before the fire could spread further. No injuries were reported among the residents, firefighters, or animals involved in the incident.

The details surrounding the cause of the fire and extent of damage to the structure have not yet been released by fire officials.

City officials in Prichard, Alabama gathered this week to hash out a $21.8 million budget that comes at a critical juncture for the municipality. Mayor and all five council members convened to discuss how the spending plan will impact various city services, particularly the police department.

The budget discussions arrive during what city leadership described as a period of transition and uncertainty for the community. While specifics on how the plan affects police operations weren't detailed, the department's funding appears to be a central concern as officials weigh competing priorities for the coming fiscal year.

According to reporting from WKRG News 5, the full scope of budget allocations and any changes to municipal services should become clearer as the council moves forward with formal approval steps.

item.title: Semmes officers mow elderly resident's overgrown yard, earn community award
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: A couple of Semmes police officers went above and beyond their usual patrol duties this week, earning recognition for helping an elderly woman tackle an overwhelming yard maintenance problem. Sergeant Brian Fillingim and Corporal Hand noticed the woman's grass and weeds had grown considerably during a call to her home. Rather than leave it at…
item.content:encoded: A couple of Semmes police officers went above and beyond their usual patrol duties this week, earning recognition for helping an elderly woman tackle an overwhelming yard maintenance problem. Sergeant Brian Fillingim and Corporal Hand noticed the woman's grass and weeds had grown considerably during a call to her home. Rather than leave it at that, the officers decided to take action themselves. "We responded to a call at her house and we realized the grass was getting really tall, so myself and Corporal Hand spoke about it when it was over," Fillingim explained. The officers' initiative didn't go unnoticed. Their work earned them the Smiles Behind the Shield Award, recognition that highlights the kind of community-focused policing that builds trust between law enforcement and the neighborhoods they serve. The gesture underscores how small acts of service—especially for vulnerable residents who may struggle with physical tasks—can make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Mobile cut the ribbon Thursday on a new senior center serving the Hillsdale community, according to WKRG News 5. The facility, named after the late John E. King—a longtime deacon and community leader in Mobile—will provide a gathering space for senior citizens in the area.

City officials and members of the community attended the opening ceremony to celebrate the new resource. The center represents an expansion of senior services in Mobile County, offering seniors in the Hillsdale area a dedicated space for activities and programming.

King's legacy as a faith leader and advocate for his community made him a fitting namesake for the center, which now bears his name.

item.title: Gulf Islands National Seashore updates personal watercraft wake zones
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The National Park Service has announced adjustments to wake zones for personal watercraft operating along the Gulf Islands National Seashore, which stretches across the Panhandle including waters off Pensacola and Santa Rosa County. According to WKRG News 5, the changes to the regulated wake zones are intended to better manage recreational boating…
item.content:encoded:
The National Park Service has announced adjustments to wake zones for personal watercraft operating along the Gulf Islands National Seashore, which stretches across the Panhandle including waters off Pensacola and Santa Rosa County.

According to WKRG News 5, the changes to the regulated wake zones are intended to better manage recreational boating activity in the protected marine areas. The seashore encompasses roughly 150 miles of pristine coastline and waters that see significant seasonal boat traffic from both local residents and visitors.

The National Park Service manages these zones to balance recreation with environmental protection, including safeguarding seagrass beds and marine habitats that are critical to the Gulf's ecosystem. Personal watercraft operators in the area should review the updated regulations before heading out on the water.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Gets $25K Grant for Cat Trap-Neuter-Return Program

item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Animal Shelter has secured a $25,000 grant from Florida Animal Friend to expand its Trap-Neuter-Return program, according to county officials.

The funding will help the shelter continue its efforts to manage the feral cat population in the county through humane methods. The Trap-Neuter-Return program catches stray and feral cats, has them spayed or neutered, and returns them to their original locations, reducing reproduction and preventing the need for euthanasia.

This grant represents a significant boost to the shelter's animal welfare initiatives in Santa Rosa County.

item.title: West Nile virus detected in Mobile County sentinel chicken
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: A sentinel chicken in Mobile County, Alabama has tested positive for West Nile virus, according to the Mobile County Health Department. The bird was part of the Vector Services program's monitoring efforts in the 36613 ZIP code area. Sentinel chickens are used by health departments across the country as an early warning system for West Nile virus…
item.content:encoded:
A sentinel chicken in Mobile County, Alabama has tested positive for West Nile virus, according to the Mobile County Health Department. The bird was part of the Vector Services program's monitoring efforts in the 36613 ZIP code area.

Sentinel chickens are used by health departments across the country as an early warning system for West Nile virus activity. Because chickens develop antibodies to the virus without typically showing severe symptoms, they help officials track the presence of the disease in specific regions before human cases emerge.

While the detection was in Mobile County, residents in nearby Escambia County and throughout Northwest Florida should remain vigilant about West Nile virus prevention. Health officials recommend using insect repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants during peak mosquito hours (dawn and dusk), and eliminating standing water around homes where mosquitoes breed.

West Nile virus is transmitted to humans through infected mosquito bites. Symptoms can range from mild fever and body aches to severe neurological complications in rare cases. Most infected people experience no symptoms at all.

item.title: Alabama launches statewide alert system Baldwin County already uses
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: Alabama this week activated a new statewide notification system designed to warn the public about life-threatening emergencies, but one coastal Alabama county has been using a similar setup for years. Baldwin County's existing emergency alert infrastructure mirrors the capabilities now being rolled out across the state, according to WKRG News 5.…
item.content:encoded:
Alabama this week activated a new statewide notification system designed to warn the public about life-threatening emergencies, but one coastal Alabama county has been using a similar setup for years. Baldwin County's existing emergency alert infrastructure mirrors the capabilities now being rolled out across the state, according to WKRG News 5.

The statewide system aims to reach residents quickly during critical situations like severe weather, hazardous material incidents, or other public safety threats. State officials highlighted the expanded reach and coordination benefits of having a unified platform across all counties.

Baldwin County's experience with its own notification system suggests the transition for other counties should be manageable, though implementation details and integration with local systems may vary by county. The state system is expected to complement existing Emergency Alert System (EAS) infrastructure that broadcasts through TV and radio.

item.content:encoded:
Two Alabama Department of Transportation employees had to be rescued after becoming suspended from the Delta Bridge over the Tensaw River when their work platform malfunctioned, according to WKRG News 5.

The incident occurred during routine maintenance operations on the bridge structure in Baldwin County. Details about the exact nature of the equipment failure weren't immediately available, but authorities responded to extract the workers from their precarious position.

ALDOT has not yet released additional information about the workers' conditions or the cause of the malfunction. The Alabama Department of Transportation typically conducts regular inspections and maintenance on major bridge structures, including the Delta Bridge, which spans the Tensaw River in the Mobile area.

No word yet on whether the incident will affect bridge traffic or upcoming maintenance schedules.

Volunteers interested in participating in the cleanup can join the effort at either of the two designated Pensacola Beach locations. The event represents a local opportunity for residents to take direct action in protecting the area's marine environment and beaches.

For Mobile listeners and Parton fans across the Southeast, the discovery of a local connection serves as a reminder of the artist's broad reach and her ability to touch people in unexpected ways.

item.title: Patronis says Jelly Roll 'not welcomed' in Panhandle after Trump jokes

Patronis, a Republican statewide official, took issue with remarks Jelly Roll made during…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Chief Financial Officer Jimmy Patronis has publicly stated that musician Jelly Roll is unwelcome in the Florida Panhandle following comments the artist made about former President Donald Trump during an appearance on The Late Show with James Kimmel.

Patronis, a Republican statewide official, took issue with remarks Jelly Roll made during the late-night television interview. The CFO's comments reflect broader political tensions in a region that remains a Republican stronghold.

Jelly Roll, a Nashville-based rapper and singer known for his chart success and advocacy work, has not publicly responded to Patronis's statement. The exchange underscores how celebrity commentary on political figures can draw swift reactions from Florida's political leadership.

It's unclear whether the artist had planned performances or appearances in the Panhandle, or if Patronis's statement was a preemptive political statement. The dispute remains a point of cultural and political friction in the region.

item.title: LUNAR ECLIPSE TONIGHT
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: You won't need special glasses to see the lunar eclipse coming to Pensacola tonight. While Florida residents won't see a total lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow — known as the umbra — will cover almost 94% of the moon. You'll have to stay up late if you want to see the peak of the eclipse, which will happen shortly before midnight, but most people…
item.content:encoded: You won't need special glasses to see the lunar eclipse coming to Pensacola tonight. While Florida residents won't see a total lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow — known as the umbra — will cover almost 94% of the moon. You'll have to stay up late if you want to see the peak of the eclipse, which will happen shortly before midnight, but most people should be able to see the start of the eclipse earlier in the evening. Of course, the best viewing will be away from lights and with no clouds. The eclipse begins: 8:23 p.m. tonight with the maximum at 11:12pm and ending around 2am.
